title: Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions
main_claim: For every fixed k>=3, r_k(N) <= C_k N exp(-c_k (log N)^{eps_k}). Equivalently, an alpha-dense subset of [N] has a k-AP once log N >= A_k(2+log(1/alpha))^{A_k}. This settles Erdos's reciprocal-sum conjecture for APs of every length, and it also implies the Green-Tao dense-primes theorem and quasipolynomial van der Waerden bounds.

issues.description: This is not a defect. It is a coverage caveat. About 9k lines of appendix proofs were not checked line by line. They contain the shift comparison, cube comparison, the relative lifting theorem behind the dimension-independent fresh rank d_0, and constrained sampling/equidistribution. The headline result depends on all of them, especially the claim that the relative lifting returns rank d+d_0 with d_0 independent of ambient dimension, and the claim that every width loss at layer j is 'warm' (independent of Q_{<=j}). Inside the main body these claims hang together, but the body does not prove them on its own.
issues.evidence: Lemma ap:absolute: 'The number of slots is at most d_0=(2+p)^C, independent of n' (relies on Theorem lifting:relative-theorem); Prop. ap:iteration:widths: 'P_j is a fixed polynomial independent of q_j and of all lower width logs'.

coverage: I read the whole main-body skeleton and checked it closely: the introduction and Corollary ap:reciprocal; Section 01 (cell definitions, Theorem ap:increment, Lemma ap:absolute proof, budget conventions); Section 08 in full (root compression, the dimension recurrence H_i = d_i + H_{i+1}^2 and its envelopes, the descending width schedule, finite-horizon closure, and the inversion to the density bound, all verified); Section 04-scalar (forward mass bookkeeping, where I checked the s_j/t_j* recurrences and the normalisations by prod e_i); and Section 03-major up to and including the rank-cut transaction lemma (own-layer width loss depends only on gap and dimension, lower losses use cold data at h, the cut count is bounded by the dimension argument). In the foundations I read Positive grids, Positive counting (I verified the B_b kernels: B_{1/4} = 3/8+3u/8+3v/8-uv/8 and E nu_i nu_i = 1-b+buu', which is positive, and the deficit bound 1+tau/16), and the fixed-dimensional absolute increment (budget exponents). I also read the inverse-theorem statement, its box and cyclic-group reductions (Phi embedding, cube-count normalisation, 4^n piece selection), and the statement of the relative lifting proposition. I checked all of Section 09 (dyadic sums, the w_{*,eta} cancellation, and the tail integral bound 2 v0^b e^{-v0}). I only skimmed or skipped Sections 02-paths, 03-relative-detection, 04-return, 05-ascent, 06-active and 07-extraction, plus most of the appendix proofs (shift comparison, cube/transfer, lifting, sampling).
